identity.title: Hyperparameter Trajectory Inference with Conditional Lagrangian Optimal Transport

problem.claim: The paper addresses learning how a neural network’s conditional output distribution changes with hyperparameters, enabling approximation at unobserved settings and adaptation to evolving post-deployment preferences without retraining.

gap.claim: Existing trajectory-inference approaches need extension to handle conditioning, which makes ensuring feasible inferred paths more difficult.

contributions.claim: A conditional Lagrangian optimal-transport approach jointly learns hyperparameter-induced dynamics, transport maps, and geodesics between observed marginals to build a surrogate model.
The learned Lagrangian incorporates inductive biases from the manifold hypothesis and least-action principles to improve surrogate feasibility.
The authors report better reconstruction of neural-network outputs across various hyperparameter spectra than alternative methods.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce Hyperparameter Trajectory Inference as a task and propose conditional Lagrangian optimal transport for constructing surrogates at unobserved hyperparameter settings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their approach reconstructs neural-network outputs better than other alternatives across various hyperparameter spectra.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hyperparameters set important neural-network behavioural trade-offs, while user preferences may change after deployment and make retraining costly.
The paper defines HTI to infer conditional output-distribution changes with hyperparameters and approximate outputs at unobserved settings.
Conditioning extends trajectory inference and complicates feasibility of the inferred paths.
Conditional Lagrangian optimal transport learns dynamics, transport maps, and geodesics, with manifold and least-action biases added to the Lagrangian.
The authors report superior output reconstruction across varied hyperparameter spectra relative to alternatives.

source_observation.claim: The abstract names the target task, identifies feasibility as the central challenge, and links specific inductive biases to that challenge.

lessons.interpretation: A compact problem–obstacle–design-rationale chain can make a technical proposal’s motivation easier to evaluate.
lessons.application: When presenting a new surrogate method, explicitly map each architectural or objective bias to the failure mode it is intended to address.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the method has no clearly articulated target failure mode or design rationale.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, output metrics, hyperparameter spectra, baselines, or numerical improvement behind the reported reconstruction comparison.
It does not provide formal conditions or quantitative evidence establishing when the inferred paths are feasible.
